mode: adapter integration on controlled fixtures; no LLM or user desktop autonomy claim
command: npx vitest run tests/browserSession.test.ts tests/mcpStdio.test.ts tests/mcp.test.ts

evidence.mechanism: Actual sandboxed Chromium opens fixture, reads DOM, fills without GET beacon or POST, exact actual POST requires native-approval callback, one approved POST reaches server; downloaded Polish text independently read from disk and SHA256 returned.
Unresolved native approval is aborted immediately; late grant cannot dispatch previous request; fixture received zero POSTs.
Deferred DNS and launch spy; STOP settles pending operation before DNS returns; late DNS produces zero launch calls. This is a startup regression unit test, not real-browser autonomy.
Real Chromium onclick changes form action and value. Native approval receives actual /mutated?target=changed GET. Denial produces no request to either original or changed destination.
Real browser discovers link; symlink download directory is rejected; independently enumerated outside directory remains empty.
Own Node SDK fixture discovers/calls ping; stalled initialize times out and child PID exits; STOP aborts actual pending call, marks effect uncertain and closes own server PID.

Mock transport regression proves remembered scopes and catalog removed, late response rejected, no extra call after revoke; arbitrary application token is not attached, redirects disabled, incorrect JSON-RPC id rejected.

evidence.case: STOP while Chromium launch is pending
evidence.mechanism: Deferred launch unit regression keeps busy/starting state and leaves STOP unfinished until owned browser resolves and closes. No false stopped:true while owned startup remains pending.

evidence.case: draft delayed GET after fragment navigation
evidence.mechanism: Actual Chromium fill schedules delayed GET. Subsequent open(#fragment) destroys old browser while its traffic remains blocked, then creates clean isolated context. Server log contains no autosave or delayed draft GET.

limitations: No real model routed these tasks through the normal JARVIS chat field. These results do not satisfy full user-agent browser/desktop acceptance gates.
Public internet browser interaction was not tested in this pass. Domain-scoped local fixture browser interaction was real.
Browser download adapter requires Linux /proc/self/fd anchoring; other platforms explicitly report PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE for download.
Browser uses an isolated ephemeral context and only an already installed configured Chromium executable; no imported user cookies or model/browser downloads.
Interactive pages may need additional exact origins. Draft filling deliberately blocks network side effects, including autosave GET requests; clicks require approval for actual outgoing requests.
MCP JSON HTTP transport rejects SSE endpoints explicitly. Stdio uses the pinned MCP SDK.
STOP cannot roll back a remote side effect already sent. Stdio cleanup controls its direct owned server process, not arbitrary daemon descendants created by that server.
No system-wide service, Cua Driver or Xvfb installed.
Opening another URL after fill/click creates a fresh isolated browser context to prevent old-document draft disclosure; temporary login/session state is not preserved across that reset.

cuaDriver.license: MIT for Cua Driver; optional cua-perception has separate AGPL/non-MIT terms and was not installed
cuaDriver.observed: cua-driver executable absent; no target authorized graphical session and no reviewed bounded capability manifest
cuaDriver.compatibility: Current Driver supports stdio MCP modern 2026-07-28 and legacy 2025-06-18, which installed MCP SDK can negotiate. Driver default standard mode is promptless; integration must use reviewed bounded mode rather than unrestricted.
cuaDriver.platformEvidence: Upstream GNOME requires Wayland user session, WinRects helper and portal grant; shared renderers/video remain open. KDE requires Plasma6, no full accepted behavioral matrix. Real Xorg /dev/uinput behavior is listed not yet validated.
cuaDriver.decision: Keep existing native X11 backend with its concrete X11/DISPLAY prerequisites; do not pretend Wayland or Cua execution. Do not admit unreviewed cua-driver command or run deprecated insecure cuabot. Installed Driver, owner-reviewed bounded manifest and target desktop remain prerequisites.
